purpose: Kill criterion 3 of the pre-registration: the signal does not ship if it costs measurable compile latency without a significant recall@1 gain. The recall gain is zero, so the cost had to be measured rather than argued.
method: harness/latency.py, serial client, 20 untimed warm-up compiles, then the first 100 corpus instances repeated; A and B alternate rounds against two servers on the same store file

builds.A: 00e21fc — branch base, byte-identical to main at 0.7.0
builds.B_first_design: 7f705a5 — evidence sources loaded for every candidate on every compile
builds.B_shipped: hasDeadHeat gate — evidence sources loaded only when the returned window holds a dead heat

first_design_rejected.note: This design tripped kill criterion 3 and was NOT shipped. Recorded because a rejected measurement that is deleted is not evidence of anything.
first_design_rejected.reading: B slower on 3 of 4 comparisons, roughly +1.4 ms p50 (+7%), against round-to-round noise of the same order. Not clean enough to call either way, but the mechanism is unambiguous: the sources query grew from top_k=5 ids to up to max_candidates=200.

shipped_design.reading: p50 differs by at most 0.35 ms (2%) and the sign is not consistent across rounds. Kill criterion 3 passes.

not_established: These are single-client, loopback, warm-cache numbers on one host. They are not a throughput or concurrency claim.
One store, one corpus. A store whose claims carry many sources would move the contested branch's cost and has not been measured.
